decisions.reason: The client criticizes the preview's overall AI-generated appearance but does not change the existing lip-sync accuracy or natural-expression requirements.
The realism complaint does not change the required actor nationality or gender preference.
The message supplies feedback obtained through the preview workflow but does not change the preview artifact, language, duration, or review purpose.
The client requires a more realistic result but does not reassign sourcing responsibility or specify a new source for footage, script, or voiceover.
The message criticizes visual realism rather than changing the reference-led creative basis or its relationship to the reference.
The realism complaint does not alter the independent sourcing or testimonial-style presentation of the testimonial material.
Although the client says the preview creates a poor impression, the source decision specifically establishes a visual-realism standard and does not change the existing viral-style requirement.
The complaint concerns visual appearance and does not change the required audio level or mixing standard.
The candidate's color grading, final polish, and native UGC finish remain required unchanged; the new non-AI-looking acceptance criterion is already owned by the visual-realism Requirement.
The visual-realism decision does not change the pilot's duration, formats, video counts, or expansion condition.
The source message does not discuss or change the integrated call to action.
The realism complaint does not change subtitle presence, quality, or mobile formatting.
